references.text: The Levites were appointed to serve at the tabernacle and take care of it, which corresponds to their duty mentioned here.
The Levites were given to Aaron to perform service at the tabernacle, but the priesthood was reserved for Aaron and his sons.
The Kohathites were not to touch the holy objects, or they would die - the same warning as in this verse.
Warning that the Kohathites must not look at the holy things, or they would die - a parallel to the death penalty mentioned here.
Only Aaron's descendants could burn incense before the Lord at the altar; others would suffer the same fate as Korah.
The Israelites were not to approach the tent of meeting, or they would incur guilt and die.
Nadab and Abihu died when they approached with unauthorized fire - an example of the consequences of unauthorised access to the sanctuary.
The priests had to wash themselves before approaching the altar, or they would die - the same seriousness attached to the sanctuary.
King Uzziah was struck with leprosy when he unlawfully entered the temple to burn incense at the altar.
Only the high priest could enter the Most Holy Place, and only once a year - illustrating limited access to the holy.
